sections.h2: What does the Mason County Register of Deeds actually keep?
sections.html:
The office holds the permanent record of every deed, mortgage and other paper that conveys or burdens land inside Mason County. The county page explains that the register is an elected county officer serving four-year terms, and that state law (MCL 565.551) requires the office to provide proper facilities so the public can inspect what it holds.

The register has a second job that surprises some owners: chairing the county plat board, which looks over proposed subdivisions before they go to the state. The county clerk serves as that board's secretary, and the county treasurer is the third member.

Three different clocks run in the office on weekdays, except legal holidays:

  • The front desk is open from 9 to 5
  • Recording stops earlier, at 4:30
  • Passport applications are taken from 9 to 3

Ask the office for its street address and direct phone line before you send a package.

sections.h2: What is Mason County like, and who is selling homes there?
sections.html:
Ludington is both the seat and the largest city, and the county started life in 1840 as Notipekago before it was renamed in 1843. Mason County reaches across 1,242 square miles, but only 495 of them are dry land, since 60 percent of the area is water. US 10 crosses the county east to west through Scottville and Custer, US 31 joins it near Ludington, and M-116 hugs the Lake Michigan shore up to Ludington State Park. Part of the Manistee National Forest lies inside the line.

The Census Bureau put the 2025 population at 29,040, nearly flat against 2020. Survey numbers for 2020 through 2024 describe an older county than its neighbors:

  • Owners value a typical house at $219,600
  • 78.3 percent of homes are occupied by their owners
  • Typical gross rent is $896
  • 28.8 percent of residents are 65 or older
  • Typical household income is $64,748

Families moving a house to a child or grandchild should know that MCL 207.526 exempts those deeds from the state tax, provided the exemption is written on the deed.

sections.h2: What will the Mason County recorder's counter charge for a deed?
sections.html:
A deed, mortgage, lis pendens or similar instrument costs $30.00 to record. A document that releases or assigns more than one instrument adds $3.00 per extra one. Plain copies are $1.00 a page, plat copies are $2.00 a page, and certifying a copy is $5.00.

Name searches by staff run 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and state or federal tax lien certificates are $3.00 per name. The county's fee page carries a February 2018 update date, so phone the office to confirm a figure before you write the check.

Images and indexes reach back to June 23, 1840 and are online now. Heavy users can buy a prepaid subscription, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The county cautions that its index is a working tool that may contain mistakes and is not a certified search.

sections.h2: How big is the transfer tax bill on a Mason County sale?
sections.html:
The county's own table adds $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500 of price, so every $500 slice carries $4.30. The grantor owes it on any deed given for $100 or more.

Mason County combined transfer tax at three sale prices, pulled from the county's published table
Price up toStateCountyTotal
$50,000$375.00$55.00$430.00
$75,000$562.50$82.50$645.00
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00

The pattern continues beyond the table's top row. A $200,000 sale has 400 slices and owes $1,720, while a $250,000 sale has 500 slices and owes $2,150. For a price that lands between rows, use the county's table.

The register keeps a separate exemption page for the county share and for the state share. Whatever exemption applies must be typed on the deed. Among the exempt transfers are foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, and land contracts where title has not yet passed.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Mason County Register of Deeds accepts it?
sections.html:
The register posts the text of MCL 565.201 on its site. For anything signed after April 1, 1997, the key points are legible signer names beneath each signature, the notary's printed name on the same page, grantee addresses, and the name and business address of the person who prepared the deed.

Layout counts too. The sheet needs a clear 2 1/2 inch strip at the top of page one, text of 10 point or larger, and paper between letter and legal length. The first printed line must name a single recordable event. English translations go on anything written in another language, and the first five digits of a Social Security number must be removed.

The statute treats an instrument that the register accepts as conforming, and the register cannot refuse a compliant deed over its contents. That is why closing agents review the deed before it is presented.

sections.h2: Who certifies taxes on a Mason County deed, and what else does that office do?
sections.html:
The county treasurer does. The treasurer's page says it certifies deeds before recording to show no delinquent taxes for the five years before the instrument date, and it provides tax histories on request. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts need the certificate, under MCL 211.135.

The office is open weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax line is 231 843-8411. Real property taxes become delinquent each March 1, when township and city rolls pass to the county at settlement. Village taxes follow a different schedule.

Mason County has been an opt-in county for tax foreclosure since 2004, so the county treasurer runs the foreclosure and sale of tax-delinquent parcels rather than the state. It also opted in to audits of principal residence exemptions, so audits of exemptions claimed in error come from that office.

sections.h2: Which Mason County office handles parcel splits and address changes?
sections.html:
The Equalization Department, open 8 to 5 weekdays at 231-845-6288. It assigns addresses everywhere except Ludington and Scottville, splits and combines tax parcels, updates mailing addresses and supplies tax maps. The county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the annual equalization report also live there.

That matters when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside piece is being divided. The register of deeds records the deed, and equalization then updates the parcel records.

Mason County owners can also join the free Property Fraud Alert service. Sign-up details are on the register's page.

faqs.q: How much does the Mason County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $30.00 per document. Extra instruments released in one document add $3.00 each. Plain copies are $1.00 a page and a certification is $5.00.

faqs.q: When does Mason County accept documents for recording?
faqs.a: Recording runs from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays except legal holidays. The front office stays open until 5 p.m. A deed arriving after 4:30 may wait for the next business day, so plan closings accordingly.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a $200,000 Mason County sale?
faqs.a: About $1,720 combined, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county. The seller owes it unless the deed carries a stated exemption.

faqs.q: Does a Mason County deed need a tax certificate?
faqs.a: A warranty deed or land contract does. The county treasurer certifies that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years. A quitclaim deed with no covenant of warranty is excused under MCL 211.135.

faqs.q: How far back do Mason County online land records go?
faqs.a: Images and indexes are online from June 23, 1840 to the present. The county calls its index a working index, so check any key detail against the recorded document.
